Bill.BriefDescription: Authorizing an additional motor vehicle registration fee to fund environmental protection or cleanup.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to a motor vehicle registration fee to fund airquality protection and improvement and motor vehicle related toxiccleanup; adding a new section to chapter 46.16 RCW; adding a newsection to chapter 70.105D RCW; adding a new section to chapter 70.94RCW; creating a new section; providing an effective date; and providingan expiration date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that: (1) Air is an essential public resource that must be preserved,protected, and enhanced for current and future generations. Improvingair quality is a matter of statewide concern and is in the publicinterest. (2) Air pollution can have adverse health effects on manypopulations in the state of Washington, particularly children. Overfour hundred thousand students in the state risk their health breathingexhaust from riding the bus to school every day. One out of every tenchildren in our state suffers from asthma. Diesel exhaust is likely tocause lung cancer in humans, chronic and acute bronchitis in children,asthma attacks, and respiratory illnesses. p. 1 HB 1762 (3) Although stringent standards established by the United Statesenvironmental protection agency for new diesel school buses will beginwith the 2007 model year, seventyfive percent of the more than eightthousand five hundred buses on the road now in the state will continueto be used for the next thirteen or more years. (4) Solutions are available to address this health risk, includinginstalling filters and oxidation catalysts on school bus engines toremove harmful emissions and using cleaner fuels such as ultralowsulfur diesel fuel, biodiesel fuel blends, and natural gas fuel.Installation of these devices and the use of cleaner fuels will reduceharmful fine particle and toxic air pollutant emissions by up to ninetypercent. (5) Money deposited in the state air quality account will be usedfor, among other purposes, installing filters and catalysts on schoolbus engines to reduce harmful emissions and using ultralow sulfur fueland biodiesel blends on the diesel school buses currently usedthroughout the state.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 46.16 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) In addition to all other fees imposed under this chapter, thefollowing registration fees shall be imposed at the time of initialregistration: (a) Ten dollars for all campers, motorcycles, or trailers; (b) Twenty dollars for all passenger cars and for hire vehicles; (c) Thirty dollars for all trucks, motor homes, combination ofvehicles, commercial vehicles, and travel trailers. (2) Vehicles licensed under chapter 46.87 RCW are exempt from thefees imposed under subsection (1) of this section. (3) The proceeds from the fee imposed under subsection (1) of thissection shall be deposited in the state air quality account createdunder section 3 of this act. (4) This section expires July 1, 2040.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.105DRCW to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The state air quality account is hereby created in the statetreasury. The following money shall be deposited into the state air HB 1762 p. 2 quality account: (a) Money which is raised by the fee imposed undersection 2 of this act; and (b) any other money appropriated ortransferred to the account by the legislature. (2) Money in the account may be used for any purpose allowableunder chapter 70.94 RCW, and the purposes of this chapter as it relatesto air pollution, including but not limited to the followingactivities: (a) The hazardous waste cleanup program required under this chapteras it relates to air pollution; (b) Reducing air contaminant emissions and cleaning up airpollution; (c) Reducing and eliminating toxic air contaminants; (d) Addressing and mitigating the impact of climate change; (e) Retrofitting motor vehicles, including school buses and transitfleets, with exhaust emission control devices; (f) Providing funding for the differential costs of cleaner andalternative fuels and vehicles which reduce air emissions and allowadvanced exhaust emission control devices to be used, includingultra-low sulfur diesel fuel, biodiesel, and natural gas; (g) Providing funding for infrastructure necessary to allow fleetsto use alternative, cleaner fuels; and (h) Administrative and operating costs of air pollution controlauthorities and, where there is no air pollution control agency, thedepartment, to develop and oversee the air pollution cleanup programsidentified in this section. (3) Money deposited in the state air quality account shall besubject to distribution as follows: (a) Eighty percent of the funds shall be distributed to the airpollution control authorities created under chapter 70.94 RCW. Thefunds shall be distributed in direct proportion with the amount of feesimposed under section 2 of this act that are collected within theboundaries of each authority, however, an amount in direct proportionwith those fees collected in counties for which no air pollutioncontrol authority exists shall be distributed to the department. (b) Twenty percent of the money deposited in the state air qualityaccount shall be distributed to the department and shall be used by thedepartment for the following purposes: p. 3 HB 1762 (i) The hazardous waste cleanup program required under this chapteras it relates to air pollution; (ii) Reducing air contaminant emissions and cleaning up airpollution; (iii) Reducing and eliminating toxic air contaminants; (iv) Addressing and mitigating the impact of climate change; (v) Retrofitting motor vehicles, including school buses and transitfleets, with exhaust emission control devices; (vi) Providing funding for the differential costs of cleaner andalternative fuels and vehicles which reduce air emissions and allowadvanced exhaust emission control devices to be used, includingultra-low sulfur diesel fuel, biodiesel, and natural gas; (vii) Providing funding for infrastructure necessary to allowfleets to use alternative, cleaner fuels; (viii) Administrative and operating costs of air pollution controlauthorities and, where there is no air pollution control agency, thedepartment, to develop and oversee the air pollution cleanup programsidentified in this section; and (ix) Hazardous waste cleanup programs related to toxic pollution orpotential toxic pollution of land, air, or water caused by motorvehicles in their use, recycling, storage, or destruction. (4) Money in the state air quality account may be spent by thedepartment only after appropriation.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.94 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Notwithstanding RCW 39.36.020(1), air pollution control authoritiescreated under this chapter may at any time contract indebtedness orborrow money for any lawful authority purpose and may issue generalobligation bonds or other evidences of indebtedness, secured by thepledge of one or more of the taxes, charges, or fees authorized to beimposed or received by the authority, including, without limitation,the state air quality account moneys to be distributed to the authorityunder section 2 of this act and money received from other private orpublic sources, in an amount not exceeding, together with any existingindebtedness of the authority not authorized by the voters, one andone-half percent of the value of the taxable property within theboundaries of the authority; and with the assent of three-fifths of the HB 1762 p. 4 voters voting at an election called for that purpose, may contractindebtedness or borrow money for authority purposes and may issuegeneral obligation bonds or other evidences of indebtedness providedthe total indebtedness of the authority does not exceed five percent ofthe value of the taxable property. The bonds shall be issued and soldin accordance with chapter 39.46 RCW. In no circumstance shall thisdebt be the obligation of the cities or counties within the boundariesof the authority.

If any provision of this act or itsapplication to any person or circumstance is held invalid, theremainder of the act or the application of the provision to otherpersons or circumstances is not affected.
